verdict: Prudential earned $1.39B as its PGIM investment arm and U.S. businesses held firm, but a sales suspension at Prudential of Japan cut that business's earnings by a quarter and pulled premiums well below last year.

segments.name: Premiums
segments.note: What customers pay for life insurance, annuities and group coverage, earned over the coverage period — down sharply from a big prior-year quarter.

segments.name: Net investment income
segments.note: Interest and dividends on the large portfolio Prudential invests between collecting premiums and paying claims.

segments.name: Policy charges & fee income
segments.note: Fees charged on policyholder accounts, such as annuity and life policy accounts.

segments.name: Asset management & service fees
segments.note: Fees from PGIM, Prudential's investment-management arm, for managing money for institutions and individuals.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — staff, technology and servicing policies and investments.

opex.name: Amortization of policy acquisition costs
opex.note: Spreading the upfront cost of selling policies (such as agent commissions) over the life of each policy.

otherDetail: A $466M loss on Prudential's catch-all 'other income' line and a $32M drop in the value of market risk benefits (guarantees attached to annuities), partly offset by $20M of realized investment gains — a net $478M drag — plus $21M of earnings from joint ventures, less $17M of profit attributable to noncontrolling interests.
footerNote: Insurer adaptation, following Prudential's own presentation: revenue here is operating revenue — premiums, net investment income, policy charges and asset-management fees ($14,927M). Market-driven lines that sit inside total GAAP revenue (other income, realized gains and market-risk-benefit changes, a net -$478M) are shown below operating income instead; total GAAP revenue was $14,449M. The cost of revenue combines policyholder benefits ($7,972M), interest credited to policyholder accounts ($1,446M), dividends to policyholders ($110M) and a -$85M change in estimates for future policy benefits. Net income is the $1,388M attributable to Prudential shareholders; total net income was $1,405M.
follow100Note: Measured against operating revenue of $14,927M, as explained in the notes below. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Japan suspension bites
takeaways.text: Japan Businesses' adjusted operating income fell to $559M from $750M as the Prudential of Japan sales suspension cut constant-dollar sales 36% and raised expenses. Prudential also agreed to sell its Brazil, Mexico and South Africa businesses to simplify the company.

takeaways.title: PGIM keeps winning money
takeaways.text: PGIM took in $9.0B of third-party net inflows — its best quarter in two and a half years — and earned $263M, up from $244M, on higher asset-management fees. Total company assets under management reached $1.62 trillion.

takeaways.title: U.S. annuity sales boom
takeaways.text: Retail annuity sales of $3.9B were the highest since 2013, with record sales of registered index-linked annuities. U.S. Businesses earned $1,173M on an adjusted basis, about flat with a year ago.

oneTimers: GAAP net income includes $368M of pre-tax net realized investment losses and related charges (including $184M of credit-related losses) and a $32M pre-tax loss from changes in the value of market risk benefits, partly offset by $295M of pre-tax earnings from divested and run-off businesses and $104M of gains from market experience updates.
Prudential's headline adjusted operating income was $1,321M, or $3.77 per share (non-GAAP) — it strips out the market-driven items above.
